All 18 playbook rules have been reviewed and submitted. Summary from our side (Corio is our party; Commerce One is the vendor/licensor):

**Deviations redlined (5)**
- **LOL-CAP** (critical): mutual cap exists but is limited to fees paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" and carves out only indemnification — reset to 12 months' fees paid or payable, plus carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and our payment obligations.
- **IP** (critical): §13.5 hands ownership of Developments we create back to Commerce One whenever it supports them — reversion deleted.
- **T4C** (high): five-year term with no convenience right — added a 30-day Corio convenience right with pro-rata refund; Commerce One gets none.
- **WARRANTY** (medium): 60 days from Effective Date with a hard 31 December 1999 cut-off — extended to 12 months (90 days as fallback).
- **TRANSITION / INSURANCE** (missing): inserted a §11.4 transition-assistance and data-return clause and a §14 vendor insurance covenant.

**Compliant (12)**: INDEMN (uncapped vendor IP indemnity covering us and our Customers), NONCOMPETE, EXCLUSIVITY, MFN, NOSOLICIT, RENEWAL (12-month renewals, 30-day window; no reminder or uplift cap — noted), GOVLAW (California law/AAA San Francisco, at fallback), ASSIGN (at fallback; competitor-consent carve-back noted), LICENSE (perpetual, irrevocable, subcontracting permitted; affiliates unnamed — noted), AUDIT, LD, MINCOMMIT.
